intent_record.intent_summary: Extend remove_nh_grp_entry to accept a deferred-free list for coordinated deferred resource cleanup.
intent_record.what: The function signature of remove_nh_grp_entry was changed to add a new fourth parameter, `struct list_head *deferred_free`, while leaving the existing parameters and local variable initialization unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this enables callers to pass a deferred-free list into remove_nh_grp_entry, allowing the function to participate in deferred cleanup or object lifetime management instead of relying only on its previous inputs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer cleanup of removed nexthop group entries by queueing them for later free instead of immediately freeing percpu stats.
intent_record.what: The change removes the immediate call to free_percpu(nhge->stats) after list_del(&nhge->nh_list), keeps nexthop_put(nhge->nh), and adds list_add(&nhge->nh_list, deferred_free) so the entry is placed on a deferred_free list instead of having its percpu stats freed immediately.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the nh_grp_entry is no longer partially freed as soon as it is removed from its current list; instead, it is queued for deferred cleanup. This prevents its percpu stats from being released too early while the entry may still need coordinated later destruction, reducing the risk of use-after-free or inconsistent cleanup ordering.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an initialized deferred-free list in remove_nexthop_from_groups() to support safe delayed cleanup of nexthop group entries.

intent_record.how: This adds an initialized empty kernel linked-list head available within the function for collecting entries to be freed later, enabling deferred cleanup logic instead of immediate freeing during group removal processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer freeing nexthop group entry percpu stats until after synchronize_net() to avoid releasing memory before RCU readers are done.

intent_record.how: This defers freeing per-CPU statistics associated with nexthop group entries until after synchronize_net() completes, ensuring RCU/network readers have finished before the memory is released and preventing premature frees during group removal.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the new RCU-visible stats usage and the freeing path in remove_nh_grp_entry(). The vulnerable construct is present: readers access nhge->stats from the group entry in fast-path selection functions via "nh_grp_entry_stats_inc(nhge)" which does "cpu_stats = this_cpu_ptr(nhge->stats);" and is called from nexthop_select_path_fdb(), nexthop_select_path_hthr(), and nexthop_select_path_res(). In remove_nh_grp_entry(), the code publishes a replacement group with "rcu_assign_pointer(nhp->nh_grp, newg);" and then immediately does "free_percpu(nhge->stats);" followed by "nexthop_put(nhge->nh);". There is no grace-period wait such as synchronize_net() between making the old nh_grp_entry unreachable for updaters and freeing the per-cpu stats. Because old readers may still be traversing the previous nh_grp array under RCU and can call this_cpu_ptr(nhge->stats), this is exactly the root-cause condition: freeing an RCU-visible nh_grp_entry's percpu stats too early. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
